Canonical AnimHeader.frameCount and AnimFrame.gfxIndex establish max gfx index plus one, which must exactly meet the independently referenced animation-table base before a full gfx table is owned. All complete animation payload bytes agree across regions. Twenty gfx tables with unresolved trailing entries stay incbin.

All five real AnimHeader prefixes and frame sequences are decoded per region; maximum gfxIndex is65 in US/EU and62 in JP. Those exact extents independently reach the animation-table base. JP localized frames differ and its gfx pointers use JP-only names, not assumed US slot correspondence.
provenance.resource_unused_suffixes: Nineteen ObjDef-referenced gfx tables have a proven used prefix bounded by max AnimFrame.gfxIndex+1 and a separate trailing group of words before the independently referenced animation-table base. The used prefix is a real void* array; each trailing word is a separate neutral void* scalar without claiming it is accessed as an array element. Every pointer target independently decodes as Sprite/OAM metadata, with all minimum consumed payload bytes identical across US/JP/EU.
